name: Maryland
summary: Maryland allows one certified plug-in system of up to 1,200 watts per utility meter. You notify your utility, but it cannot require approval or charge fees.
watt_cap_note: Per utility meter, one system per meter.

tiers.rule: Exempt from certain product-listing and code provisions that would require altering the building.
Must be certified by UL or an equivalent national testing lab.

certification: UL or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory.

utility.notification: You must notify your utility after installing. It is a notice, not an approval.

renters: Sources conflict. One report says landlords cannot block a device but tenants must give notice; another says the law is silent. Get written permission until this is verified.
open_questions: Effective date: it passed as an emergency bill (effective on signing, May 12, 2026) per the fiscal note, but one guide says July 1, 2026.
Whether landlords are barred from prohibiting devices.

sources.title: HB 1532 fiscal and policy note, Dept. of Legislative Services
pv magazine: plug-in provisions pass in Maryland and Colorado
